title: Where Did the Word OK Come From?
hook: You say it every day. It’s one of the most widely understood words on Earth. And it started as a joke.

segments.n: In 1830s Boston, newspaper writers loved playing with abbreviations and funny misspellings. It was the internet slang of its day.

segments.n: In 1839, a Boston paper used O.K. as shorthand for oll korrect, a joke misspelling of all correct.

segments.n: Most of those jokes faded fast. But this one got lucky. In 1840, a political campaign gave it a second life.

segments.n: Supporters of Martin Van Buren, nicknamed Old Kinderhook, used O.K. as a slogan. After that, it never left.

segments.n: A joke misspelling became a global word. What everyday word do you use that started as a joke?
